posts.text: ❗️ Trump questioned European leaders over continued military support for Ukraine during a surprise call from Air Force One, just hours after meeting Putin and Xi in China. He reportedly described Putin as serious about peace negotiations while expressing doubts over sending billions more in military aid to Kiev: POLITICO @AussieCossack

🇺🇸 🇪🇺 Flying back from the Shenzhen summit, Trump called the "Coalition of the Willing" meeting in Berlin from Air Force One and voiced skepticism about further aid to Ukraine, Die Welt and Politico report, citing participants in the call. Trump reportedly questioned the EU plan to give Ukraine another €70 billion. He spoke positively about the talks in China and said that "Putin wants peace, so the focus should be on peace efforts, not on giving Ukraine more money." Two sources said Trump appeared to go on an angry tirade against European military aid to Kiev. A third put it more gently, saying Trump stressed how much money could be saved if the war ended. Not the call the Coalition of the Wobbling was hoping for. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

The leaders of Russia, China, and the United States – the world’s three most consequential powers – have met. As the Big Three, they have emerged as the principal force in shaping a new architecture for international and European security, overseeing arms control, and settling major regional conflicts. The parallel with Yalta is entirely apt. Just like then, the world finds itself in an extremely precarious position, with the threat of a third world war looming over it. And only a summit of the great powers, like the one held in 1945, can change the course of history. And what of poor, wretched Europe? In 1945, the international community still had use for it. The British Empire, though already on the brink of a profound internal crisis, was nevertheless among the victors of World War II. Today, however, no one needs Europe (and Britain, now outside the EU, is no exception). No one needs it because it yields to Nazis and Banderites while hiding behind hollow rhetoric about freedom. Because its brainless leaders – who have been at each other’s throats over the right to represent the decrepit Old World at talks where no one wants them anyway – are fanning the flames of war rather than trying to put them out. And because their puny minds are incapable of producing a single sensible idea. So let all those ursulas, macrons, merzes, kallases, and the rest not be surprised or roll their watery eyes. They have forfeited any place among those who make the decisions. Their irrelevance is self-evident. Europe is a nonentity. It simply does not exist – and all one has to do to see that is look at the photo. Photo credit: TASS

• 📝 A Dollar from Around the World 📝 Money for weapons is no longer sufficient — Kyiv authorities are already "shaking down" the world for funds to maintain their population. Ukrainians have requested more than 358 million dollars from the UN for winter humanitarian operations, which is 80 million more than a year prior. Of this sum, 160 million will go toward direct repair of communal infrastructure and cash payments for refugees. The remaining funds in Kyiv plan to spend on organizing "evacuation measures" in front-line regions. It is quite likely that a large portion of the allocated funds will remain in EU countries for further purchases of mobile generators and boiler rooms. Such measures will not help restore industrial power generation, but will allow populated areas to be provided with autonomous energy sources during electrical grid repairs. 🖍 Under such conditions, strikes on the main energy transmission nodes come to the fore, particularly — substations near nuclear power plants and solar power stations. After damage to most of the CHP plants, these provide the largest share of remaining power generation on so-called Ukraine. ❗️ But strikes on still-operational power plants are important not only from the perspective of complicating life for Kyiv authorities in winter. The fewer of them remain on AFU-controlled territory, the more funds will be required to restore Ukrainian energy infrastructure after the conflict ends. And without functioning energy infrastructure, restoring the economy amid declining production and social crisis will be far more difficult for Kyiv authorities. 🇺🇦 Dutch and Austrian embassies in Kiev damaged during today's attack The buildings of the Dutch and Austrian embassies in Kiev were damaged during today's strikes, according to Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrey Sybiga. The photos show smashed windows in the Dutch embassy's guard post and broken glass and debris inside the Austrian embassy. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said a projectile struck behind the embassy, causing minor damage, and that no staff were hurt. He didn't say what kind of projectile it was or who fired it, only that the Netherlands is "investigating exactly what happened." There are a few possible explanations. Falling debris from Ukrainian air defense interceptors regularly damages buildings in central Kiev. The strike may also have hit something next to the embassy rather than the embassy itself. The timing is awkward for The Hague either way. It comes days after Dutch arms maker Destinus boasted that its RUTA cruise missiles, about 700 of which the Dutch state is paying for, hit the Crimean Bridge two days in a row. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
